grh_3f5517334cd5621da40f.title: Jackpot
paragraphs: Bill and Amy Lawrence seem to strike it rich when Bill wins a radio jackpot made up of thousands of dollars in merchandise, only to discover that the prizes create a huge income-tax bill and almost no cash to pay it. Bill desperately tries to sell everything from soup to watches, loses his job in the process, and nearly wrecks his marriage when Amy mistakes artist Hilda Jones's secret portrait of her for evidence of an affair. A recovered $5,000 payment for a lost prize gives the family enough to meet the tax crisis, Bill lands an even better job, and the couple finally escapes for a vacation. When another giveaway program calls, they refuse to answer and want nothing more to do with jackpots.

[[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Anne Diamond, Betty Lou Gerson, Bill Bouchey, Bing Crosby, and Bob Hope. Other credited names include Bill Cairn as director, Howard Wiley as producer, Jack Rubin as radio adaptor, and Jimmy Wallington as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 60 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.0ee8343bca2245d4|Chesterfield]] and [[org|org.47c43e9eb0213c63|RCA]].
This version presents a radio version of [[work|work.sdp.film.3c72d419af19e752|Jackpot]]. Jack Rubin adapted it for radio.

grh_3f5c486c84cfaca8b9b4.title: The Mercenaries
paragraphs: Veteran mercenary Colonel Fest is hired by commercial interests to overthrow President Andre Bocar of Mondunga, the ruler Fest himself helped install a year earlier. With only a small force, Fest combines infiltration, a fake foreign-aid offer, a seized radio station and promises of back pay and bonuses to turn the army and presidential guard without a conventional battle. The coup succeeds and a former president returns, but the new regime immediately begins planning executions and proves no more principled than the old one. Fest is unconcerned: he demands the rest of his fee, the defense ministry and a share of the saffron business, making clear that money, not liberation, has driven the operation from the start.

[[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Alan Caillou, Lloyd Bochner, Antoinette Bower, Marvin Miller, and Ben Wright. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, Alan Caillou as writer, and [[person|howard-duff|Howard Duff]] as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_3f146ea90de2d4b4fac1.title: Three Skeleton Key -Antony Ellis
paragraphs: Three lighthouse keepers on Three Skeleton Key are besieged when a derelict ship releases an enormous horde of starving rats onto their isolated tower.
